_inactive_examples._comment: Not used by any client: unknown top-level keys are ignored. Copy an entry into mcpServers to activate it (README: MCP Client Configuration, docs/oauth.md: MCP clients).

postgresql-oauth._comment: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC (OAUTH_ISSUER + OAUTH_PUBLIC_URL on the server): the client finds the identity provider through /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and logs the user in itself. Only the URL is configured. With a pre-registered public client the id is passed on the command line: claude mcp add --transport http --client-id <client-id> postgresql <url>

postgresql-oauth-static-token._comment: OAuth access token as static header (scripts, tests). It expires (minutes to an hour), so this is not for daily use by people.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <access token of the identity provider>

postgresql-own-credentials._comment: Client-supplied connection, mode 'credentials' (token field client_connection, assignment client_connection or PG_CLIENT_CONNECTION): the bearer token authorizes the client, X-Pg-User / X-Pg-Password log in with the person's own database account on the target of the token. Use HTTPS; the headers are sent on the initialize request and apply to the whole session.

postgresql-own-database._comment: Client-supplied connection, mode 'full': the client also chooses the target (X-Pg-Host, -Port, -Database, -Ssl) and must supply user and password.
